*** US-558 CLOSED passes:true -- three navigational overlays now paint var(--bg); both confirm modals keep their 0.6 scrim; #dtc-takeover untouched. Full AC-by-AC detail in sprint.json completionNotes; reusable lessons below. ***

**A DISCOVERY-DRIVEN GUARD FAILS BY WHAT IT NEVER EXAMINED, NOT BY A WRONG VERDICT.** My CSS rule-walk had TWO silent defects and both reported SUCCESS while seeing almost nothing. (a) A comment contains no braces, so an un-stripped `/* ... */` reads as part of the NEXT rule's selector and that rule drops out of the walk -- nearly every rule in this sheet is commented, so that is the NORMAL case, not an edge one. (b) `@keyframes` closes with a `}` at column 0, so a selector pattern whose first-char class admits `}` swallows the following selector -- and `#dtc-takeover` is declared immediately after a keyframes block, so the takeover itself vanished. **Generalise: when a test DISCOVERS its own subjects, the walk needs its own tests, separate from the model that consumes them. A model can only be wrong about what it was handed.** I caught both only because I ran the suite RED first and read which failures were the defect vs which were mine.

**CLASSIFY, DON'T ENUMERATE -- it is the same durable shape as US-563's schema guard.** The story asked for three alphas. Three alphas is a fix that holds until the next overlay. What ships instead: the guard discovers every stacked full-screen layer (position:fixed + inset:0 + z-index) and REFUSES any that carries no role, in BOTH directions (an unclassified layer is drift; a classified selector the sheet no longer declares is an allowlist quietly widened for a rule that is gone). Cost was ~20 lines over the enumerated version.

**EXCLUDE ON A REAL DISTINCTION, NEVER BY NAME.** `#screen` is `position: fixed; inset: 0` and paints `var(--bg)` -- a laxer predicate sweeps it in and it PASSES the destination check for entirely the wrong reason. It is excluded because it declares no z-index (it is the frame the others stack ON), and that boundary case has its own test so the exclusion cannot become a coincidence.

**A MECHANICAL SWEEP WOULD HAVE WEAKENED A SAFETY SURFACE.** 'Every full-screen overlay gets var(--bg)' would have written a field into `#dtc-takeover`'s BASE rule, sitting under the WATCH/MINOR/UNKNOWN gradients and silently degrading the AREA channel US-484-b built the STOP tier on. Its base rule declares NO background ON PURPOSE. **Pin an out-of-scope neighbour as an ABSENCE -- then 'I did not touch it' is a property of the sheet instead of a sentence in a close note.**

**TWO ASSERTIONS THAT FAIL FOR DIFFERENT REASONS BEAT ONE COMPOUND ONE.** Destinations are checked for resolved ALPHA (so 'solid' is about opacity, not spelling) AND for TOKEN BINDING (so `rgba(0,0,0,1)` cannot pass by being opaque while re-landing a literal). Either alone leaves a real hole.

**GUARD A SCRIM ON BOTH SIDES.** `0 < alpha < 1`, not `alpha != 1`: fully transparent is no scrim at all. And assert the two confirms scrim at the SAME strength by reading both out of the sheet rather than pinning 0.6 -- what must not happen is DRIFT, and pinning the literal would forbid a legitimate tune.

**A CRUDE GUARD CAN FAIL A COMMIT THAT IMPROVES ITS OWN METRIC.** US-509's `test_dashboardCss_drillDownOverlayCarriesNoRawColourLiteral` slices 1800 raw chars from `#sys-detail` and bans `#` -- it reads COMMENTS and SELECTORS as hex. It went red on my cross-reference comment, on a commit that REMOVED a raw literal. Then my note explaining the workaround contained three more hashes and went red again. **Filed TD-084 + worked around under the scope fence rather than rewriting US-509's assertion: it fails LOUD and in the SAFE direction (it can never pass a real hex), so that is debt to schedule, not a defect to fix inside another story's fence.** If you touch dashboard.css within ~1800 chars of `#sys-detail`, do not write a bare hash in a comment.

**ANSWER THE PRIOR STORY'S PM FLAG EXPLICITLY, EVEN WHEN IT DOESN'T BITE.** BL-034 (kiosk renders at 1280x720) cannot invalidate US-558: opacity is DIMENSIONLESS. Saying that in one line is much stronger than not mentioning it.

ENVIRONMENT (re-confirmed): PowerShell tool does NOT support heredocs for python -- Write a temp .py and run it. `git commit -m @'...'@` (single-quoted here-string, closing delimiter at column 0) DOES work. **pytest prints NO summary line in this repo's config** -- gate on `$LASTEXITCODE` plus 'zero F/E characters in the progress output', not on a 'N passed' string. tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 915 tests, ~4-5 min -- run it FOREGROUND (TD-059). `Glob` on `specs/UI/**/*.css` TIMED OUT on this share; `git ls-files | grep` answered the same question instantly. Index lock CLEAR all session.

*** US-556 CLOSED passes:true -- kebab visual box vs hit box + the .menu-head fix. Full AC-by-AC detail in sprint.json completionNotes; reusable lessons below. ***

**THE STALE NUMBER IN AN AC IS NOT ALWAYS THE WHOLE AC -- RE-DERIVE AND THE PREMISE MAY SPLIT.** I was warned AC-1's "28px bar" was stale. Re-reading it against 34 did not just update a number: it revealed the AC described TWO defects and US-557 had already cured ONE of them. --fs-primary is 34 and --bar-h is now 34, so the GLYPH exactly fills the band; only the 40px BOX still overflows. I found it because a negative self-test I wrote went RED on an assertion I expected to pass, and I re-read the assertion instead of deleting it. **Generalise: when a self-test fails in the direction you did not predict, the model is usually right and your restatement of the story is wrong.**

**"EXACTLY FLUSH" IS NOT "SAFELY INSIDE".** A 34px line box in a 34px band has zero margin, and glyph INK is not bound by a `line-height: 1` box. So the glyph half still deserved fixing even though the strict inequality no longer failed. Assert `<` not `<=` when the quantity is a paint bound.

**DERIVE THE SIGNED SHORTFALL INSTEAD OF LANDING TWO LITERALS.** Iris specced `inset: -6px -7px` -- correct arithmetic for a 28px box, wrong for the 34px one. `inset: calc((var(--bar-h) - var(--tap-min)) / 2)` is HALF THE SIGNED SHORTFALL: negative while the band is under the minimum (grows the target by exactly the missing px, hit box == --tap-min), positive if the band ever exceeds it (pseudo shrinks inside, button already over the minimum). Self-correcting BOTH ways. **When a spec hands you two magnitudes, ask what they are the difference between -- the subtraction usually belongs in the sheet.**

**AUDIT BY WHAT A CONTROL PAINTS, NOT BY THE BOX IT RESERVES.** I nearly modelled AC-4 as "no control's box exceeds its band" -- which would have flagged `.dot` (a 40px box in a 16px band) as a fourth defect. `.dot` is CORRECT: its box is transparent + border-less and its mark is an 8px `::before`. That is the precedent my whole fix rests on, and it was already in the sheet. **Check whether the sheet already solved your problem before inventing a mechanism; then pin the precedent, so a later change to it invalidates your citation loudly.**

**THE SAME DEFECT CAN HAVE OPPOSITE CORRECT FIXES.** #menu-btn shrinks to its band; `.menu-head` GROWS to its control. Not inconsistency -- #topbar defends a 320px stage budget US-557 just fought for, an overlay head defends nothing. **Ask what the band costs before deciding which side moves.**

**A PASSING TEST CAN STILL BE A STALE MEASUREMENT.** US-555's bar-width model charged the kebab at `--tap-min`. After my change it charges 40 for a 34px box -- green, and wrong, and an OVER-estimate so it would never have gone red. Moved the pin to read the declared width, and made the helper ASSERT the declaration is a `var()` (a bare literal would give a plausible number and re-create the drift). **Green is not evidence a model still measures its subject.**

**`position: relative` IS THE QUIET FAILURE ON ANY ::after HIT-AREA.** Without it the pseudo anchors to the nearest positioned ancestor -- here #topbar, which is `position: fixed` -- and the hit area lands somewhere else while every other assertion passes. It needs its own test, because nothing else in the file can see it.

**READ THE PRIOR STORY'S PM FLAG BEFORE BUILDING, THEN SAY WHY IT DOES OR DOESN'T BITE.** US-560 flagged that the kiosk renders at 1280x720, which could invalidate canvas-budgeted chrome work. It does not bite US-556 -- every claim here is a RATIO inside the uniformly-scaled 480x320 #stage, so it holds at any output mode and BL-034 cannot invalidate it. Saying that explicitly is much stronger than not mentioning it.

ENVIRONMENT (re-confirmed): PowerShell tool does NOT support heredocs for python -- Write a temp .py and run it, then delete it. `git commit -m @'...'@` (single-quoted here-string, closing delimiter at column 0) DOES work in the PowerShell tool. **pytest prints NO summary line in this repo's config** -- `-q` gives dots only, so gate on `$LASTEXITCODE` plus "zero F/E characters in the progress output", not on a "N passed" string. tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 888 tests, ~4-5 min -- run it FOREGROUND (TD-059). A `PostToolUse` security hook flags `eval()` in new files; an `ast.parse` + whitelisted-node walk is ~15 lines and avoids it entirely. Index lock CLEAR all session.
